study.question: Why did the 70-slot uniform-readout control improve over its 30-slot predecessor, and can keeping structured normalization support while blocking its preactivation gradients improve click AUC without added parameters?
study.hypothesis: Observed: g0-r0021-target_partition_uniform reached 0.6666620368383296 versus 0.6659300360390669 for its original-population bridge (+0.0007320007992627), while aligned and rotated readouts scored 0.665610891151665 and 0.6659935372855875. Source inspection shows the uniform readout is unchanged algebraically; the four extra rows per block enter Dice batch moments, running state and normalization-mediated gradients. Provisional mechanism: extra target-conditioned support rows can stabilize the activation distribution, but their backward contributions can steer shared scorer and item embeddings away from the actual uniform readout. Treating those support preactivations as constants before each Dice may retain useful forward normalization with less optimization interference. This hypothesis is unconfirmed, and the prior gain could be generic population reweighting or a seed-specific result.

nearest_work.difference: Archived exact-version primary text, section 5.2 lines317-335: Dice uses mini-batch mean/variance and moving averages at inference. Local activation pooling and Dice are inherited. Proposed change is explicit control over nonreadout compressed support rows and their layerwise preactivation gradients, not a new Dice activation or an originality claim.

Pinned primary implementation lines25-34 uses BatchNorm1d(affine=False, eps=1e-9, momentum=0.01). We retain it exactly, altering which compressed rows supply its support and where their backward flow is stopped. No global nearest-priority search or broad novelty claim is asserted.

Nearest local architecture: original first three strata plus matched and valid-rank-rotated pairs, all scored before uniform-only primary selection. New attached/aligned cell reproduces it; blocked cells detach only extra-row preactivations before each Dice. Population replacement duplicates the rotated pair at identical cardinalities.

Same learned modules and five residual summaries with the original 30-slot scorer population. This older comparison motivates normalization attribution but cannot alone separate moments, running buffers and cross-row gradients.

inherited_components: All authorized frozen field embeddings, target/action-aware DIN scorer and four task towers from g0-r0021-target_partition_uniform.
Ten temporal blocks; original uniform and feedback/nonfeedback slots; exact target-ID matches with padding/OOV exclusion and valid-rank rotation.

Five inherited task-specific residual summaries including ordinal and quadratic details and gated duplicated match direction; residual width16, zero final-layer initialization and source RNG behavior.
Original auxiliary-only scorer/item stop-gradients, train-time cloned Dice buffers and 30-slot auxiliary scoring; four fixed BCE objectives.
study.proposed_difference: A complete 2x2 with no learned additions: (1) aligned-plus-rotated support versus two copies of the count-matched rotated support; (2) ordinary backward flow versus stop-gradient of extra support preactivations immediately before EACH Dice in the primary scorer. Always score 70 rows and read only uniform means. Keep first three strata attached. At a fixed state, gradient pairs must have identical training forward values/running-buffer updates and identical evaluation outputs. Extra-row moment contributions remain; their backward paths into preceding layers are blocked. This is a partial-gradient optimization operator, not deletion of support or a claim that all normalization gradients disappear. Earlier evidence already includes failed compressed task-query replacement (0.659194 versus events-task 0.660163), match-detail task/shared contrast (0.663019 versus0.661646), useful ordinal blocks (0.665011 versus duplicate0.663220), and unsuccessful joint/cubic/feedback extensions whose duplicates or bridges won. These multiple trajectories favor checking a concrete normalization confound over assuming more detail helps.
predictions: At fixed parameters and identical batches, attached and blocked cells of either population have equal primary outputs, Dice moments and running-state updates; support preactivation adjoints are zero only in blocked cells. First three row adjoints remain admissible; auxiliary-only scorer/item gradients stay zero and context gradients remain permitted.
support_aligned_attached reproduces g0-r0021-target_partition_uniform at the frozen seed, modulo documented host nondeterminism; parameter/module and initialization parity must be exact.

If the optimization hypothesis is useful, support_aligned_blocked improves primary click AUC over support_aligned_attached and both frozen source bests; all-task metrics and costs are reported even if auxiliary quality degrades.

If aligned support provides more than population multiplicity/count information, aligned blocked exceeds rotated blocked at matched parameter count, support row counts and per-block cardinalities. The corresponding attached comparison and factorial difference assess dependence on backward flow.

The expected parameter count remains32129765 total/336549 dense/31793216 embedding in every cell. There is no extra scorer pass; stop-gradient masks may affect memory/runtime, so measured cost rather than equal FLOPs alone decides efficiency.
falsifiers: No click-AUC gain of aligned blocked over its attached bridge falsifies the predicted advantage of this gradient intervention for this implementation; a one-seed improvement remains preliminary.
Rotated duplicate support matches or exceeds aligned support in both gradient settings: evidence does not support target-aligned value grouping beyond inherited count information.
If all 70-slot alternatives similarly exceed the historical 30-slot source, generic normalization-population weighting remains sufficient; do not claim aligned compression is responsible.

Any changed forward value/buffer update within a fixed-state gradient pair, changed count/empty-slot pattern within a population pair, failed source parity, masking leak, prohibited auxiliary gradient, nonfinite forward/backward, or mismatched learned initialization invalidates attribution pending diagnosis.
An apparent quality gain explained by higher measured cost, adverse auxiliary changes or subsequent paired-seed failure does not establish a general unified-model improvement.
alternative_explanations: Changed Dice training moments, accumulated running statistics, and partial backward dynamics are distinct pathways; this round does not isolate training moments versus inference buffers.
Count-dependent empty-slot mixtures and duplicated support weighting can explain the prior gain without aligned semantic support. Rotation preserves cardinality but can preserve some semantics.
Shared scorer updates and sparse embedding updates are jointly affected by layerwise detach; further ownership controls would be required for that attribution.

The single frozen seed, adaptive validation reuse across many trajectories and weak auxiliary AUCs limit generalization and significance. Baseline/source comparisons are contextual when architecture differs.

A stop-gradient change could act as generic regularization rather than fixing task conflict. Auxiliary performance has deteriorated relative to DIN, so click gains do not imply multi-task Pareto improvement.
